commands.name: scene_add
commands.description: Adds a scene with this name to OBS's current scene collection (Scenes › Add, the name, OK).

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": OBS has no scripting for this.

example_requests: Add a scene called Intro in OBS
Make a new OBS scene for the interview
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: OBS's scene collection has the scene.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the result wasn't seen in time

errors.name: AlreadyExists
errors.when: a scene with that name exists; nothing is done

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: an OBS dialog is open, or another app came to the front; nothing more was done

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with OBS Studio 32.0.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
On OBS's first launch its question about checking for updates is answered Don't Check, and after OBS quit unexpectedly its Safe Mode question is answered Run in Normal Mode.
It doesn't add sources to the scene.

commands.name: recording_start
commands.description: Starts recording with OBS's current scene and output settings (Controls › Start Recording).

args.name: allow_blank
args.meaning: If the scene has no video source OBS warns it will record a blank screen: True answers Yes, False answers No and raises StateBlocked.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": OBS has no scripting for this.

commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: OBS is recording into its recordings folder (by default ~/Movies).

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the result wasn't seen in time

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: OBS is already recording, the scene has no video source and allow_blank is False, an OBS dialog is open, or another app came to the front

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with OBS Studio 32.0.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
On OBS's first launch its question about checking for updates is answered Don't Check, and after OBS quit unexpectedly its Safe Mode question is answered Run in Normal Mode.
Capturing the screen, a window, a game or a camera needs macOS permissions that these commands never ask for, so add such sources yourself; testing recorded the empty scene with Mic/Aux.
On a Mac with a microphone, OBS's default Mic/Aux source may make macOS ask for Microphone access; the test VM has none, so that prompt wasn't seen, and these commands don't answer it.

commands.name: recording_stop
commands.description: Stops OBS's recording (Controls › Stop Recording) and returns the file it wrote.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": OBS has no scripting for this.

example_requests: End recording and tell me where the video is
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: The recording file is complete in OBS's recordings folder.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the result wasn't seen in time

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: OBS isn't running or isn't recording; nothing is done

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with OBS Studio 32.0.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
The file is found as the newest video in OBS's recordings folder (from its profile settings) written in the last 15 seconds.

commands.name: source_add
commands.description: Adds a new color or text source to OBS's current scene (Sources › Add, the kind, Create new with the name, OK, its properties, OK).

args.name: name
args.meaning: The new source's name; no other source or scene may have it.

args.name: text
args.meaning: The text to show; required for kind="text", not allowed otherwise.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": OBS has no scripting for this.

example_requests: Add a text overlay saying Live in 5
Put a color background in the OBS scene
Add a caption source to OBS
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: The current scene has the source, saved in OBS's scene collection.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the result wasn't seen in time

errors.name: AlreadyExists
errors.when: a source or scene with that name exists; nothing is done

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: an OBS source dialog or properties window is open, or another app came to the front; nothing more was done

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with OBS Studio 32.0.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
On OBS's first launch its question about checking for updates is answered Don't Check, and after OBS quit unexpectedly its Safe Mode question is answered Run in Normal Mode.
Text uses OBS's default font, color and size; a color source keeps OBS's default color.
Image, media, capture and camera sources aren't offered: OBS didn't take an image path typed through Accessibility, and capture needs macOS permissions.
